persons.name: Joseph Clizbe
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Clizbe, Joseph' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). persons.name: Stephen F. Gale
persons.note: Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named'. It gives a name, a trade and usually an arrival year, and it is a retrospective of 1884: a YEAR off it is documented, a MONTH is not, and it says nothing whatever about 1835. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago, 10 August 1833 — “Gale, Stephen F.” (poll_1833_011, line 32). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Gale' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). OLD SETTLERS, 1879 — A DATE THIS MAN GAVE FOR HIMSELF, AND STILL NOT A FACT ABOUT 1835. The Calumet Club's FIRST reception to the settlers of Chicago prior to 1840, 27 May 1879, printed its register in the proceedings (Early Chicago, Chicago, 1879, pages 84-90), and this man's entry reads “Gale, Stephen F. | 1835, May, | Exeter, N. H. | 67 | Chicago.” — name, his own date of arrival, his birthplace, his age and his 1879 post-office address, in the register's five columns. The date of arrival is HIS RECOLLECTION, set down forty to sixty years after the event; the address is where he lived in 1879 and is never read as an 1835 residence. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json).

No figure is drawn (L1). THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Jordan, James O. | Letter. | October 30, 1872. | Dismissed.” (second_presb_0651, printed page 191), admitted 1872-10-30 by letter. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Jordan' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins J. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

No figure is drawn (L1). THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Thacker, Mrs. Anna Rommeiss | Letter. | March 21, 1888.” (second_presb_0330, printed page 172), admitted 1888-03-21 by letter. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Thacker' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins A. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” THE LINE IS A MARRIED WOMAN'S ENTRY, and the crosswalk's own Mrs rule governs what it can have met: “a line flagged a_married_womans_entry that meets a MAN in the 1835 layer has met his name, not him: it corroborates that the name was a Chicago name in the 1840s and it does not put that man on this roll.” The match is filed rather than suppressed, because a suppressed match is invisible and a flagged one can be argued with. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

persons.name: Me Tai Wa
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1376, stage `underdocumented`). Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `ME TAI WA`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_065#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. No figure is drawn (L1).

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive. H-family house massing currently resolves through the frame dwelling archetype; no larger house generator is implemented. THE CENTRE HALL IS THE ENTRY'S, NOT THIS PARCEL'S (T-1686). H1 is the only family of the thirty-five whose crosswalk entry names a centre hall and states a bare bay count — its required variant is "center_hall_one_and_half" and its variants line reads "5 bays; center hall; kitchen ell; small porch" — so the plan and the bay count below are read off that entry and not dealt by this parcel. The kitchen ell and the small porch the same line offers are NOT raised with them: both are selectable variants beside the required one, and an ell is a footprint fact this record's rectangle does not carry.
